label: mid-input m/r/j/p/y/k/a after a w/v/s/l/n/c-initial sequence
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase: 98.5% of mass, peaking at t=3..5. It never fires at t=0-1 or at the delimiter, and very rarely during copy. The current input token is mostly m (7.5x lift, the strongest and the top activations), r, j, p, and less so y, k, a; it is usually that token's first occurrence. Firing depends strongly on context: the sequence starts with w/v (4.7x), or s/l/n/c, and earlier inputs from {w,v,c,x,s,u,d} raise the rate. The highest activations are m or r at step 4-6 after prefixes like "w n v c y". The predicate (input in that token set, t>=3, first token in {w,v,s,l,n,c}) gets about 0.46 F1 and 0.65 mass recall on dev. Misses are other tokens (e, t, o, f, 0) in the same favourable contexts, plus sequences starting with other tokens. False positives are those tokens when the prefix holds unfavourable tokens such as k, f, z, 1, o, g. This looks like a graded hidden-state context gate, not a crisp rule.
